answer: Charge each identity a proof-of-bandwidth every epoch: random peers stream it data and it must relay the full volume back inside a window, its throughput lit like a beacon the peers measure directly. One honest agent serves its single thread of traffic over one real uplink. A farm cannot fold a thousand heads onto one pipe: measured bandwidth is shared, so each head's throughput falls as heads multiply, and the cipher of random peer-assignments blocks time-slicing one link across many. N identities demand N real uplinks at once; bandwidth does not batch.
